derek-tran.text: Says 'healthcare should be a right, not a privilege'; supports lowering health and prescription-drug costs, opposes Medicaid cuts, and supports defending Medicare.
Supports 'a living-wage minimum wage' and 'cutting taxes for middle-class families and small businesses.'
Opposed H.R. 4776 (the SPEED Act) and supported restrictions on new West Coast oil and gas leasing.
Describes himself as '100% pro-choice'; co-sponsored the Right to Contraception Act, the Women's Health Protection Act, and the EACH Act.

Says 'the United States is strengthened by immigration' and opposes 'unchecked or abusive ICE practices'; backed H.R. 9883 letting families sue private ICE detention centers. Voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act.
Supports universal background checks, an assault weapons ban, and increased investment in violence prevention.
Original cosponsor of H.R. 14, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act; supports early voting, vote-by-mail, and automatic voter registration.
Voted Yea on the Stop Insider Trading Act.

chuong-v-vo.text: Says 'Government wastes money too easily'; opposed a 2020 Cerritos sales tax increase, arguing the city could balance its budget without it.

source.title: From Cop to Mayor to Congress: Chuong Vo's Case for Common-Sense Government

chuong-v-vo.text: Would address affordability by 'cutting wasteful government spending and auditing agencies for waste and fraud'; signed the Americans for Tax Reform Taxpayer Protection Pledge against tax increases.
Cites rising crime as a motivation for running; wants a 'common sense' approach and says 'Results matter more than rhetoric.'

source.title: From Cop to Mayor to Congress: Chuong Vo's Case for Common-Sense Government

chuong-v-vo.text: Supports body-worn cameras, de-escalation training and community policing; says 'We don't need more racial profiling.'
Says environmental policy should 'protect clean air and water without punishing families, small businesses, or driving jobs' and favors 'cleaner technology while keeping energy affordable.'
Wants to 'secure the border and restore order, then modernize legal immigration,' with faster asylum and visa processing and 'professional enforcement without racial profiling.'
Supports 'requiring proof of citizenship to vote as a safeguard' while saying voting 'should remain easy and states should retain flexibility.'
Says 'Parents should be partners in education' and supports improving reading, math and science and expanding career and technical education.
Publicly identified as pro-life; recommended by the California ProLife Council as its 2026 candidate.
